title: So kannst du deine KI-Sichtbarkeit messen
author_source: Lili Frankus (duwerk), OMR Reviews ContentHub, 23.01.2026, Blogpost (Gastbeitrag)
note: Practical how-to for auditing brand visibility in ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini: builds a prompt set, defines KPIs (brand mentions, citations, citation frequency, prompt coverage, visibility share, sentiment, factual correctness) and shows how to filter AI referral traffic in GA4 with a regex. Recommends starting with four KPIs. Written by a GEO agency founder, so it partly promotes the agency's own services.
course_use: German pre-reading for an 'AI visibility' module of a brand audit; students run a mini prompt-set audit for a brand and compare share of voice with competitors. Access: free.

title: Künstliche Intelligenz: Wie misst man Markenpräsenz in LLMs? Mattes Schrader hat die Lösung
note: Reports on a tool from Oh-So Digital (Matthias 'Mattes' Schrader) that tracks how brands perform in LLM answers along the AIDA phases and turns this into competitor rankings. Shows how a funnel logic from classic brand tracking is being carried over to AI search. Paywall: only the teaser is free.
course_use: Discussion hook: can funnel-based brand tracking be carried over to LLMs? Pair with the free OMR how-to. Access: paywall (HORIZONT+).

title: Warum KI bessere Marketingziele braucht
author_source: ADZINE guest author (former Appinio market researcher, now agency media planner), W&V, 03.08.2026, Gastbeitrag
note: Argues that AI-driven optimisation will maximise whatever short-term KPI it is given, so brands should adopt mental availability or mental market share as the shared goal metric. Cites a meta-analysis of 100+ brands with r = 0.83 between mental market share and sales; the study is not named, so verify it before use. Soft paywall.
course_use: Discussion hook on which KPI a brand audit should make the 'north star'; have students check the 0.83 claim against Romaniuk's Better Brand Health. Access: paywall (W&V subscription), with some full text visible.

title: Was Marken im Optimierungsdruck aus den Augen verlieren
author_source: Stefan Schasche, W&V, 17.08.2026, Artikel (with Olaf Peters-Kim, Welect)
note: Argues that constant campaign optimisation favours short-term efficiency metrics, so a campaign can look efficient while the brand wins few new buyers. Makes the case for reach, mental availability and new-customer acquisition as brand-health indicators. Paywall after the intro.
course_use: Short German hook on the 'short-term metrics trap' when choosing audit KPIs. Access: paywall.

title: Mark Ritson: "People don't give a fuck about your brand"
author_source: Conrad Breyer, W&V, 24.06.2026, Artikel (Cannes Lions report)
note: Report on the joint Ritson and Byron Sharp session at Cannes Lions 2026, where they presented five 'marketing truths' (mental availability, distinctive assets, low consumer involvement). This is a separate piece from Breyer's later column 'Zehn Jahre statt 40 Tage', which is already in the guide. Paywall after the intro.
course_use: German entry point to the Sharp and Ritson positions; use with the English Ritson columns already in the guide. Access: paywall.

title: Marketingexperte Mark Ritson: Warum sich CMOs nicht wie Kinder verhalten sollten
note: Ritson argues that erratic CMO decisions (frequent repositioning, new campaigns and agencies) cost both awareness and sales, and that consistency in brand management pays off. Includes his '10 harsh truths' for advertisers and announces his regular HORIZONT column. Paywall.
course_use: Discussion hook for the 'consistency' dimension of a brand audit, i.e. how often assets and positioning changed. Access: paywall.

title: Kolumne von Mark Ritson: Die deutschen Verbraucher verstehen mehr von Werbung als die deutschen Marketer
note: Ritson's German-language column on the gap between what German consumers expect from advertising and what German brands deliver, aimed at the DACH marketing industry. Paywall; the free teaser contains no data.
course_use: Optional German Ritson column for discussion on the DACH market. Access: paywall.

title: Nummer eins im Kopf
author_source: markenartikel – Das Magazin für Markenführung, Ausgabe 10/2026, Artikel (with Stefanie Sonnenschein, Interrogare)
note: Article on measuring mental availability, Byron Sharp's key driver of brand growth, featuring the market research institute Interrogare. The teaser notes that the approach long lacked a valid data foundation in practice. Paywall: only the teaser is visible, so the study design was not checked.
course_use: German practitioner perspective on putting mental availability into brand tracking. Access: paywall (markenartikel subscription).

title: Der Sprung ins kalte Wasser: Von dem Wagnis, ein Brand Tracking für eine große Marke umzustellen
note: In-house researcher's account of switching the brand tracker of a large brand. Covers running old and new providers in parallel and calibrating historical waves, effects of panel composition and survey bots, cutting a 20+ minute questionnaire to about 20 core questions, question-order effects, and the client complaint that trackers yield no actionable decisions. Note: planung&analyse has moved, and the URL now redirects to marktforschung.de/planung-analyse, so find the article there.
course_use: Strong case for the 'tracking design' session, on comparability, wave calibration and data quality. Access: login/paywall likely; the URL redirects.

title: Grow your brand: Wie ein Framework für evidenzbasiertes Markenwachstum aussieht
note: German framework article built on Sharp: penetration (share of buying households) as the core KPI, mental and physical availability as drivers, and the Distinctive Asset Grid (unprompted testing of static, moving and sound assets among category buyers) as the audit tool. Gives the rule of thumb of 4–5 highly distinctive assets. The URL now redirects to marktforschung.de/planung-analyse.
course_use: German pre-reading on the Ehrenberg-Bass audit logic (penetration, availability, asset grid). Access: login/paywall likely; the URL redirects.

title: Neuer Markenauftritt von Jaguar: Die Katze macht Beute
note: Contrarian strategist view that the Jaguar rebrand ('Copy Nothing', new monogram, leaper largely retired) was a success, against design critics who saw it as a break with the brand's core. Useful counterpoint for a rebranding post-mortem. Paywall.
course_use: Debate exercise on Jaguar: assign this pro view against the absatzwirtschaft and PAGE critiques, then check the later sales figures. Access: paywall.

title: Paukenschlag von Jaguar: Radikales Redesign der Traditionsmarke!
note: Design-press documentation of the Jaguar identity: mixed-case wordmark, monogram, gold palette, and the 'Copy Nothing' spot without a car. Frames the shift from selling cars to selling a lifestyle and records the first meme and backlash reactions. Gives primary visual material for analysing which distinctive assets were dropped.
course_use: Free visual source for a distinctive-asset audit of Jaguar before and after the rebrand. Access: free.

title: Rebranding von Jaguar: The cat is dead. Long live the cat!
note: Column calling Jaguar the most-discussed rebrand of 2024. It assesses the wordmark as defensible, criticises the monogram sharply, and calls the coordinated launch communication a marketing coup because awareness came before any car was shown. Note: absatzwirtschaft URLs currently redirect, so the link could not be fetched.
course_use: Second German Jaguar view for the post-mortem debate. Access: probably free or registration; the link redirects at present.

title: Etablierte Firmen verlieren bei den 150 stärksten Marken Österreichs (BrandAsset Valuator 2025)
note: Austrian BAV 2025 by Scholz & Friends Wien: about 1,000 brands, 12,500 respondents aged 16–69, brand strength measured on Differentiation, Relevance, Esteem and Knowledge, plus 49 image attributes and 80+ value questions. Findings: ChatGPT rising; Apple and Manner losing strength; top 3 are Amazon, Österreich and Google.
course_use: Austrian benchmark data for a brand-audit exercise: place a local brand on the BAV pillars. Access: free.

title: "Brand Finance Top 25"-Report: Das sind die wertvollsten und stärksten Marken Österreichs 2025
note: Brand Finance Austria 25 (2025): brand value defined via the licensing (royalty-relief) logic, separate from brand strength (BSI). Red Bull is most valuable, Erste Bank strongest, ÖBB second on strength. BILLA brand value is up 70% to EUR 2bn and it enters the top 10, a useful data point for discussing the Merkur to BILLA Plus brand consolidation.
course_use: Use to contrast financial brand value with brand strength, and as an outcome check for the BILLA/Merkur case. Access: free.

title: Supermarktkette Merkur wird in Billa Plus umbenannt
note: News source on REWE retiring the Merkur brand in favour of BILLA Plus: cost savings, ending internal rivalry, facade changeover from April 2021, supplier fears of 'Hochzeitsboni', and loss of variety for consumers. Gives the stated rationale for a brand-architecture decision.
course_use: Case anchor for an Austrian rebranding post-mortem (rationale in 2021 compared with Brand Finance 2025 BILLA growth). Access: free with consent banner or ad-free login (PUR).

title: Marktagent: Das sind Österreichs Top-Marken
note: Describes Marketagent's Brand.Diamonds mobile tracking tool: about 1,200 brands, 270,000+ interviews, and an index of brand closeness, loyalty, USP and emotional brand character. Category winners include Milka, WhatsApp and LEGO. Shows an Austrian continuous brand-tracking design.
course_use: Example of an Austrian commercial brand-health tracker; students critique its index dimensions against MDS or mental availability. Access: free.

title: Studie: Kampagne steigert Markenbekanntheit und Consideration von Magnum
note: Short Austrian example of campaign brand-lift measurement (Teads Brand Pulse, Mindshare): awareness gain 38% above benchmark and a 10% consideration uplift. Sample and design are not disclosed, which is a good prompt for critical evaluation of vendor brand-lift studies.
course_use: Critical-reading exercise: what is missing to make this brand-lift claim credible? Access: free.

title: Wie stärke ich meine Marke?
author_source: Sabine Kaa-Pickel & Katrin Schlegel, Kantar Deutschland (Inspiration/Brand Growth), 28.02.2024, Blogpost
note: Explains Kantar's Meaningful–Different–Salient framework (BrandZ) and its four forecast metrics: Demand Power, Pricing Power, Activation Power and Future Power. Claims include 5x sales for high demand power and a 13% price premium for high pricing power. These are vendor claims, not independently verified.
course_use: German summary of the MDS audit model, to contrast with the Ehrenberg-Bass mental-availability approach. Access: free.

title: GfK Brand Architect: Durchbruch bei Messung und Management der Markenstärke
note: Describes an implicit brand-strength measure based on simulated alternative purchase decisions (consideration, preference, willingness to pay more), combined into a Brand Strength Index. It is positioned against stated trust and sympathy trackers. Vendor source.
course_use: Example of a behaviour-based alternative to attitudinal tracking in brand-audit method design. Access: free.

title: Marken des Jahres 2024
note: Shows how YouGov BrandIndex works: daily tracking of 16 metrics for 1,600+ German brands. The ranking index averages six metrics (quality, value, impression, recommendation, employer image, satisfaction) on a scale from -100 to +100, using only brands tracked over the full year (1,072 brands, 33 categories). PayPal is the overall winner.
course_use: Shows students a public continuous brand-health tracker and its index logic; ask which metrics a brand audit would add. Access: free (full ranking download may require registration).

title: Marken-Studie bescheinigt SWM und N-Ergie schlechten Markenauftritt
author_source: Pauline Faust, ZfK – Zeitung für kommunale Wirtschaft, 05.12.2025, Artikel
note: Reports the 'Brand IQ' audit of the 10 largest German energy brands by Mutabor and The Relevance Group. It is an outside-in audit using only public data across CI coherence, design quality, digital readiness, AI visibility, strategic clarity and cross-channel communication, scored on an IQ scale (Eon 117, SWM and N-Ergie at the bottom). Weak AI visibility across the sector. Subscription site.
course_use: Concrete example of an outside-in brand audit scorecard that students can replicate for an Austrian sector. Access: paywall (text partly visible).

title: Markenführung: Es muss nicht immer ein Rebranding sein
note: Decision guide for refresh versus rebrand: check brand fundamentals (loyalty, image, engagement, sales), review the design system and brand language, update the style guide, interview stakeholders, survey customers on the logo and reputation, and set concrete goals. Logo, colours and typeface should normally stay untouched in a refresh. Older but practical.
course_use: German checklist for the 'recommendation' step of a brand audit (refresh or rebrand?). Access: free.

title: Die wertvollsten Marken: Alle Rankings, Berechnungsmethoden und Entwicklungen auf einen Blick
note: Compares Interbrand, BrandZ, Brand Finance and Semion valuations, showing how far they diverge (Google at USD 114bn vs 43.5bn). Groups monetary methods into income-, cost- and market-price-based and contrasts them with consumer-based rankings. Introduces ISO 10668. Figures are from 2010, but the method comparison is still useful.
course_use: German background reading for the Markenwert session: why rankings disagree. Access: free.

title: Byron Sharp on the legacy of How Brands Grow – and why he disagrees with Les Binet
author_source: Ehrenberg-Bass Institute (marketingscience.info), excerpt of a WARC interview, ca. 2020, Interview
note: Sharp reflects on ten years of How Brands Grow (penetration over loyalty, mental and physical availability) and on his disagreement with Les Binet. The page is an excerpt; the full interview is on WARC (paywall). English.
course_use: Primary Sharp voice for the Sharp vs Binet/Field debate behind brand-audit KPI choices. Access: free excerpt; full text WARC paywall.

title: Why brands matter more than customers' enthusiasm
author_source: Dave Winterlich (Dentsu) interviewing Byron Sharp, via marketingscience.info (orig. Irish Times), Sept. 2022, Interview
note: Sharp on evidence-based marketing that can be presented to CEOs and CFOs, and on why broad brand reach matters more than the enthusiasm of loyal heavy buyers. Short and accessible. English.
course_use: Short English pre-reading on why audits should look beyond loyal-customer satisfaction. Access: free.
